module_title: Crucial Extensions - PDF, Image Formats (JPEG/PNG), and Text
introduction: This intermediate tier steps slightly outside of MS Office to cover universal web and document extensions. You must memorize the full forms of PDF and image formats, as these are mainstays in SSC CGL and Banking IT Officer exams.

core_concepts.title: .pdf (Portable Document Format)
core_concepts.description: Developed by Adobe, this is a universal file format. Its greatest advantage is that it completely preserves the original fonts, images, and layout of a document, regardless of which device or operating system is used to open it. It is generally non-editable.

core_concepts.title: .jpeg or .jpg (Joint Photographic Experts Group)
core_concepts.description: The most widely used image format on the internet and in digital cameras. It uses 'Lossy Compression', meaning it drastically reduces the file size of a photograph to make it easy to upload/download, though it sacrifices a tiny bit of image quality.

core_concepts.title: .png (Portable Network Graphics)
core_concepts.description: A highly popular image format specifically designed for the web. Its greatest feature is that it supports 'Transparent Backgrounds' (meaning an image, like a logo, can be placed over another color without a white box surrounding it).

core_concepts.title: Basic Text Formats (.txt and .rtf)
core_concepts.description:
- `.txt`: The default extension for 'Notepad'. It contains pure, raw text with absolutely zero formatting (no bold, no colors, no images).
- `.rtf` (Rich Text Format): The default extension for 'WordPad'. It allows basic document formatting (font sizes, colors) and is universally readable across different word processors.

important_entities.name: GIF (Graphics Interchange Format)
important_entities.significance: An image format famously known for supporting basic animations (silent, looping, short moving pictures). Internet 'Memes' are frequently shared in this format.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: PDF is NOT a Microsoft Format
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because modern MS Word has a 'Save as PDF' button, students incorrectly assume PDF is an MS Office extension. It is not. PDF is strictly an Adobe proprietary format.
Examiners may try to confuse you by listing both. Technically and functionally, `.jpeg` and `.jpg` are the exact same format and behave identically.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever an exam question mentions an image file format that supports a 'Transparent Background', the answer is unequivocally PNG.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the full form of JPEG precisely. Examiners will try to trap you with options like 'Joint Photo Experts Group' or 'Joint Photography Experts Group'. The exact correct word is 'Photographic'.
